name: Sishtagurunathar (Pasupatheeswarar) Temple, Tiruthuraiyur
deity: Shiva as Sishtagurunathar (Pasupatheeswarar), with the goddess Poongothai Nayaki (Sivaloka Nayaki)
period: Shaiva shrine of the Nadu Nadu country, sung by Sundarar in the Tevaram (8th century); structural temple of later date
summary: Sishtagurunathar, the Pasupatheeswarar of Tiruthuraiyur, is a Shiva shrine of the Nadu Nadu country praised by Sundarar in the Tevaram, remembered for the Lord who ferried the saint across a flooded river and taught him the way of penance.

sections.history: Tiruthuraiyur, a village north of Panruti in the Cuddalore country, is one of the Shiva shrines of the Nadu Nadu region sung in the Tevaram, and so a Paadal Petra Sthalam. Tradition counts it the fifteenth of the Nadu Nadu temples praised in the hymns, and here it was the saint Sundarar who sang, honouring the Lord in a single decad. The Lord is worshipped as Sishtagurunathar — the noble teacher — and as Pasupatheeswarar, the lord of all souls, while the goddess is honoured as Poongothai Nayaki, also called Sivaloka Nayaki. The name Sishtagurunathar is drawn from the legend of this very shrine, where the Lord is remembered as the one who taught Sundarar the discipline of penance. Built in stone by later patrons of the Tamil country, the temple has been kept in worship ever since.
sections.architecture: The temple is entered not beneath a towering gateway-tower but through a single modest gateway, unusual among the shrines of the region, within which a path leads past the flagstaff, the offering-pedestal, and the mounted Nandi to the sanctum. There the Lord stands as a large linga, worshipped as Sishtagurunathar, and the goddess Poongothai Nayaki is honoured in her own shrine. The temple's sacred tree is the kondrai, the golden-flowered Indian laburnum beloved of Shiva, and its sacred tank is named the Surya Pushkarini, the pool of the sun. In the first days of the Tamil month of Chithirai the evening sun is said to send its light into the sanctum to fall upon the Lord.
sections.legends: The great story of Tiruthuraiyur is Sundarar's. Travelling from Tiruvennainallur, the saint came to the river in full flood and could find no way across. He stood on the bank and prayed, and sang a hymn to the Lord of the shrine; in answer Shiva and Parvati came to him in the guise of an aged couple and ferried him over the water. When he had crossed, a voice from the sky bade him look up, and he beheld the Lord and the goddess seated upon the bull as Rishabarudar, revealed in their true form. In another telling the saint asked to be taught the rule of penance, and the Lord instructed him in it; and so the Lord is praised as Sishta Gurunathar and as Thava Neri Aaludayar, the master of the path of austerity.
sections.festivals: The temple's principal festival is the Brahmotsavam of the month of Vaikasi, kept over ten days around Vaikasi Visakam in May or June. Skanda Sashti and the Annabhishekam, the anointing of the Lord with cooked rice, are observed in the month of Aipasi in October or November, and Maha Shivaratri is kept in Masi in February or March, with the monthly Pradosham honoured at dusk. Dates follow the Tamil calendar, so confirm them locally before setting out.
sections.experience: Tiruthuraiyur is a quiet village temple away from the great pilgrim routes, and rewards an unhurried visit. Enter through the single gateway, walk past the Nandi to the sanctum of Sishtagurunathar, and turn to the goddess Poongothai Nayaki in her own shrine; many devotees walk also to the Surya Pushkarini, the tank named for the sun. The story of the Lord who came as an old boatman to carry Sundarar across the flood feels close at hand here, and the temple keeps the gentle stillness of the Nadu Nadu country.

visit.timings: Commonly open in the morning, roughly from six to ten, and again in the evening from about five to eight; confirm timings locally before visiting, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected: dhotis or trousers for men, sarees, salwar kameez, or long skirts for women, with shoulders and knees covered. Footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally permitted in the outer courtyards but prohibited inside the inner sanctum, in keeping with Tamil Nadu temple rules. Ask temple staff before photographing rituals or priests.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruthuraiyur lies in Cuddalore district, about nine or ten kilometres north of Panruti by way of Pudupettai and Chinnapettai. Panruti is the nearest town and railway station, and Cuddalore, the district headquarters, is around forty kilometres away. Buses and local transport serve Panruti, from where a local vehicle reaches the village.
